def-qa-37-certified-matrix-input:
## Definition

Fix $d\in\{2,5,8\}$ and put
$$SU(d)=\{T\in M_d(\mathbb C):T^*T=I_d,\ \det T=1\}.$$
A **certified $SU(d)$ matrix input** is an exact target $T\in SU(d)$ together
with a deterministic Cauchy-name procedure which, on unary input $1^b$ for
$b\ge1$, returns a rational complex matrix $Q_b$ such that each real and
imaginary coordinate of each entry differs from the corresponding coordinate
of $T$ by at most $2^{-b}$. The interface also specifies a worst-case bit-time
bound $t(b)$ for the query. A **polynomial-time name** has
$t(b)\le(b+1)^c$ for some fixed integer $c\ge1$. The target is the matrix
specified by the entire Cauchy name; if two targets satisfy the same bounds,
every coordinate difference is at most $2^{1-b}$ for all $b$, hence is zero.
No individual $Q_b$ is required to be unitary or special unitary. A requested tolerance is a positive binary
rational and its numerator/denominator encoding length is recorded
separately. For $d=2$ this specializes the unary-name convention of
[[def-qc-effective-unitary-matrix-input]]. For $d=5,8$ it is the same
entrywise interface in the fixed block dimensions; no dimension is input to
an algorithm as an unbounded parameter.
lem-qa-37-product-error:
## Statement

Let $U_1,\ldots,U_m$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ be unitary operators on the same
finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and suppose
$\|U_j-V_j\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_j$ with $\epsilon_j\ge0$. With empty
products equal to the identity and empty sums equal to zero,
$$\|U_m\cdots U_1-V_m\cdots V_1\|_{\rm op} \le\sum_{j=1}^m\epsilon_j.$$
thm-qa-37-output-distribution-error:
## Statement

Let $U,V$ be unitary operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let
$\rho$ be any density operator, and let $\mathsf M$ be any finite POVM. If
$\|U-V\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$, then the outcome distributions obtained by
measuring $U\rho U^*$ and $V\rho V^*$ have total-variation distance at most
$\epsilon$.
def-qa-37-anyon-task-and-promise:
## Definition

Work in a fixed unitary braided fusion category and fix an ordered finite list
of simple charge labels, a parenthesized fusion tree, and a total charge for
which the fusion space is nonzero. Simple charges, multiplicity bases, and
admissible fusion-tree vectors have the conventions of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. A **finite anyon decision task** is a
promise pair $(Y,N)$ of disjoint sets of binary strings with domain
$D=Y\cup N$, together with a finite encoding of admissible fusion-tree input
labels; a solver must answer yes on $Y$ and no on $N$, with no obligation
outside $D$. A **finite anyon search task** is a domain $D$ and a finite-string
witness relation, with a valid witness required only for encoded inputs in
$D$. The input record states the number and order of strands, the exact Artin
word over positive and inverse generators available to the solver, and the
finite set of adjacent fusion-measurement locations. Braid action is the
mathematical unitary action specified by the fixed physical-interface record
[[def-qc-tqc-physical-braid-interface]]; a measurement location is interpreted
in the declared fusion-tree basis. This is a finite access model, not a claim
that a physical device prepares the input or realizes the braid. Input length
and correctness-on-promises follow [[def-qa-task-and-promise-domain]].
def-qa-37-fusion-input-encoding:
## Definition

Fix $n\ge1$, ordered simple charges $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, a total charge $c$,
and one parenthesized binary tree. An **encoded fusion input** consists of the
finite tree shape, a simple-charge label on each internal edge, and a
multiplicity-basis index at each trivalent vertex. A label is **admissible**
exactly when every chosen vertex index belongs to the specified basis of its
multiplicity space $V_{xy}^z$; the allowed local vertex data and resulting
orthonormal fusion-tree vectors are those of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. The input encoding uses fixed self-delimiting
binary codes for charge labels and nonnegative multiplicity indices, with
out-of-range labels rejected as invalid encodings. It also records the total
charge and the chosen computational subspace isometry when one is supplied,
as in [[def-qc-tqc-fixed-charge-encoding]]. An encoded tree is finite classical
data; it does not itself prepare a quantum state or assert a preparation
cost.
def-qa-37-resource-cost-model:
## Definition

For a finite anyon solver instance and one run, record separately the tuple
$$\bigl(L_{\rm in},\ |b|,\ N_{\rm meas},\ b_{\max},\ t_{\rm cl},\ \epsilon_{\rm op},\epsilon_{\rm tr},\ell_{\rm leak},\ p_{\rm leak},\ N_{\rm phase},\ t_{\rm phase}\bigr).$$
Here $L_{\rm in}$ is the complete input-description bit length; $|b|$ is the
number of braid-generator occurrences (inverse generators count as one);
$N_{\rm meas}$ is the number of fusion measurements; $b_{\max}$ is the
largest unary precision query to a certified matrix name; $t_{\rm cl}$ is
the classical bit time used by search and postprocessing; $\epsilon_{\rm op}$
is a stated operator-norm approximation bound; $\epsilon_{\rm tr}$ is a
separately assumed in-band transport bound; $\ell_{\rm leak}$ and
$p_{\rm leak}$ are leakage amplitude and probability bounds; and
$N_{\rm phase},t_{\rm phase}$ count phase corrections and their classical
control cost. Circuit description and elementary wire costs follow
[[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]], while classical input bit cost follows
[[def-qa-classical-bit-cost]] and finite nonoracle gates follow
[[def-qa-nonoracle-gate-cost]]. An inapplicable coordinate is marked “not
applicable”; it is not assigned value zero. Unless an interface explicitly
states a bound, no braid length, matrix precision, measurement, search step,
or phase correction is free. The tuple is a bookkeeping convention; it does
not assert any of its error or runtime bounds.
def-qa-37-fusion-measurement:
## Definition

Let $H$ be a fixed finite fusion space with an orthonormal fusion-tree basis.
For an adjacent pair of leaves or a declared adjacent pair of subtrees, recouple
the tree by its specified unitary $F$-moves so that the pair fuses first. For
each allowed simple total charge $a$ of that pair, let $P_a$ be the orthogonal
projection onto the span of basis vectors whose pair label is $a$, transported
back by the inverse recoupling unitary. Distinct channel subspaces are
orthogonal and their direct sum is $H$, so $(P_a)_a$ is a finite projective
measurement in the sense of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]]. Its outcome is
$a$, its unnormalized branch vector on input $\psi$ is $P_a\psi$, and the
measurement is specified by the braid/F-matrix action convention in
[[def-qc-tqc-braid-action-from-fusion-data]]. The branch vector is unnormalized until its probability is checked.
def-qa-37-n-triple-fusion-code:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and $c\in\{1,\tau\}$ with $V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, using the
left-associated tree for both fixed-charge spaces. In the ordered list of
$3n$ Fibonacci $\tau$ charges, group consecutive leaves into $n$ triples;
within each triple fuse its first two charges and then its third, and fuse the
$n$ triple outputs by the left-associated $n$-leaf tree to total $c$. Restrict
each triple output to $\tau$; its two local paths are indexed by the charge
$x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two leaves. Fix a rebracketing sequence
of associators from this grouped tree to the fixed left-associated $3n$-leaf
tree, and let $R_{n,c}$ be the induced composite unitary. For each tensor
basis vector $e_{x_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{x_n}\otimes v_\lambda$, where
$e_1,e_\tau$ are the local triple paths and $v_\lambda$ is a basis vector of
$V(\tau^n\to c)$, map it to its grouped fusion-tree basis vector, then
apply $R_{n,c}$. Extend linearly and call the resulting map $J_{n,c}$. Its
image is the code $\mathcal C_{n,c}$ and it is an isometry; set
$P_{n,c}=J_{n,c}J_{n,c}^*$ for the code projector.
The factor $V(\tau^n\to c)$ retains all spectator fusion paths and is not a
physical preparation at zero cost.
def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost:
## Definition

For the fixed Fibonacci convention, write $\rho(b)$ for the physical braid
matrix and $B(b)$ for the normalized word matrix obtained by removing the
common exchange scalar $R_1$ from each Artin generator, as in
[[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]]. If $e(b)$ is exponent sum, then
$$\rho(b)=R_1^{e(b)}B(b).$$
On the three-anyon total-$\tau$ block the SK alphabet instead uses the
special-unitary lifts $zB_j$ with $z=e^{3\pi i/10}$, so a word of exponent sum
$k$ satisfies
$$\rho(b)=(R_1z^{-1})^k\widehat B(b),\qquad \widehat B(b)=z^kB(b).$$
A **phase reference record** stores the exact generator scalar, exponent sum,
which normalized convention was compiled, the resulting scalar on each
coherently used branch, and any correction operation and its declared cost
under [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A standalone fixed-sector computation
may report its output projectively using the metric of
[[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]]. In coherent control the active
branch scalar is relative to the inactive branch and must remain in the
record. No phase correction is assigned zero cost unless its interface says
so. This ledger distinguishes the common $R_1^{e(b)}$ phase from the
additional $z^{-e(b)}$ needed when the compiled alphabet is the SU(2) lift.
lem-qa-37-local-braid-acts-trivially-on-:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $c\in\{1,\tau\}$, and consider the fixed fusion space
$V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$ with its grouped tree of $n$ consecutive triples and
outer triple-charge tree. Its orthogonal decomposition is indexed by local
triple outputs $a_i\in\{1,\tau\}$ and has factors
$$\left(\bigotimes_{i=1}^n V(\tau^3\to a_i)\right) \otimes V(a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n\to c),$$
with zero-dimensional summands omitted. A braid word supported on the
internal three strands of the $i$th triple acts on this summand as
$\rho_{a_i}(b)$ on $V(\tau^3\to a_i)$ and the identity on every other local
triple factor and on the outer spectator factor. Reassociating to the fixed
left-associated $3n$-leaf tree conjugates this operator by a unitary; its
operator norm and the stated local-factor action are preserved.
thm-qa-37-fusion-branch-validity:
## Statement

Let $(P_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}$ be the finite fusion-channel projectors of
[[def-qa-37-fusion-measurement]] on a finite-dimensional fusion space $H$,
and let $\psi\in H$ be a unit vector. The channel probabilities
$p_a=\|P_a\psi\|^2$ are nonnegative and sum to one. If $p_a>0$, the
conditional branch is the unit vector $P_a\psi/\sqrt{p_a}$. If $p_a=0$,
then $P_a\psi=0$ and no normalized conditional state is defined.
alg-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-block-pair-compi:
## Definition

**Inputs:** certified Cauchy names for targets $T_5\in SU(5)$ and
$T_8\in SU(8)$; a positive binary-rational tolerance $\varepsilon$; and the
fixed normalized six-strand Fibonacci B6 generators in both total-charge
blocks. Enumerate all finite Artin words over the six-strand generators and
their inverses, and at stage $s=1,2,\ldots$ inspect every word of length at most $s$ and every
precision $p\le s$ not previously inspected, in fixed lexicographic order. For each word $b$ and precision $p$, compute rational complex
matrix approximants $P_{5,b,p},P_{8,b,p}$ to its exact normalized block
matrices and request rational target approximants $Q_{5,p},Q_{8,p}$. Each
real and imaginary entry error in these approximants is certified at most
$2^{-p}$. For $d\in\{5,8\}$ compute the rational number
$$s_{d,b,p}=\sum_{i,j}\Bigl(|\Re(P_{d,b,p}-Q_{d,p})_{ij}| +|\Im(P_{d,b,p}-Q_{d,p})_{ij}|\Bigr).$$
Return the first word for which both rational tests
$$s_{d,b,p}+4d\,2^{-p}<\varepsilon\qquad(d=5,8)$$
hold. Output the word, its exponent sum, both rational certificates, and the
measured search/precision costs in the ledger of
[[def-qa-37-resource-cost-model]]. The braid matrices have computable
algebraic entries from the fixed Fibonacci $F/R$ data
[[lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-b6-path-projectors-and-artin]]. This is a dovetailed
partial search definition: no cutoff or useful word-length/time bound is
asserted here. A separate theorem in this pair proves termination under certified target
access. The returned matrices are
normalized by the common $R_1$ scalar; their physical phase is recorded by
[[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]].
def-qa-37-finite-adiabatic-braid-input:
## Definition

A **finite adiabatic braid input** consists of a finite-dimensional complex
Hilbert space $V$, a $C^2$ Hermitian path $H(s)$ on $0\le s\le1$, a
norm-continuous constant-rank orthogonal spectral projection $P(s)$ onto a
coherently followed band with uniform positive full gap, a slow-time schedule
$T>0$, and an explicit initial isometry $A_0:\mathbb C^m\to\operatorname{ran}P(0)$.
These are the path and propagator hypotheses of
[[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]]; the output propagator $U_T$ solves
$iU_T'(s)=TH(s)U_T(s)$. Also supply an endpoint isometry
$A_1:\mathbb C^m\to\operatorname{ran}P(1)$ and a specified Fibonacci braid
word $b$ with physical action $\rho(b)$ under the fixed convention of
[[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]]. The **in-band transport condition** is a
separate hypothesis
$$\|P(1)U_T(1)A_0-A_1\rho(b)\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm tr}.$$
The phase of $\rho(b)$ is recorded by
[[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]]. This condition is not a consequence of a
projector-leakage estimate. The model also specifies a finite output
measurement and, if needed, its own implementation-variation bound. The JRS expression and leakage consequence are handled as a separate result.
lem-qa-37-fixed-sector-global-phase:
## Statement

For every Fibonacci braid word $b$ with exponent sum $k$, its physical
operator differs from the normalized operator by the common scalar
$R_1^k$ on every fixed-charge block. On the three-anyon SU(2)-lift alphabet
$zB_j$, the corresponding scalar is $(R_1z^{-1})^k$. The scalar leaves
uncontrolled fixed-sector measurement probabilities unchanged; under a
coherent control it is a relative phase and cannot be discarded without a
phase-reference correction.
thm-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-compiler-termina:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every certified Cauchy input pair
$(T_5,T_8)\in SU(5)\times SU(8)$ and every positive rational
$\varepsilon$, the exhaustive compiler of
[[alg-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-block-pair-compiler]] halts with one six-strand
Fibonacci braid word whose normalized total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
matrices are each within operator norm $\varepsilon$ of $T_5,T_8$,
respectively. Density proves termination, but this result gives no useful
joint-block word-length or search-time bound.
thm-qa-37-jrs-leakage-bound:
## Statement

For a finite adiabatic braid input with rank-$m$ spectral band and schedule
$T>0$, define
$$A_m(s)=\frac1T\left[\frac{m\|H'(0)\|}{g(0)^2} +\frac{m\|H'(s)\|}{g(s)^2} +\int_0^s\left(\frac{m\|H''(r)\|}{g(r)^2} +\frac{7m\sqrt m\|H'(r)\|^2}{g(r)^3}\right)dr\right].$$
Then
$\|U_T(s)P(0)U_T(s)^*-P(s)\|\le A_m(s)$, and every unit initial band
vector has leakage probability at most $A_m(s)^2$. In particular,
$\|[I-P(1)]U_T(1)A_0\|_{\rm op}\le A_m(1)$ and leakage probability is at
most $A_m(1)^2$. This result does not prove the separate in-band transport
condition or identify band transport with Fibonacci $F/R$ data.
lem-qa-37-fibonacci-su2-lifts-are-dense:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the fixed Fibonacci convention
$B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,r)$, $B_2=FB_1F$ with
$r=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. Put $z=e^{3\pi i/10}$ and let
$\Lambda=\langle zB_1,zB_2\rangle\le SU(2)$. Then $\Lambda$ is dense in
$SU(2)$ in operator norm.
lem-qa-37-total-error-budget:
## Statement

Let $A_0$ and $A_1$ be the initial and endpoint isometries in a finite
adiabatic braid input, let $V$ be the ideal logical unitary, and let $W_c$ be
a compiled logical unitary. Suppose
$$\|W_c-V\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_c,\qquad \|P(1)U_T(1)A_0-A_1V\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm tr},$$
and let the JRS leakage amplitude be bounded by $A_m(1)$. Fix a finite POVM $\mathsf M$ on the physical output space. If the
implemented measurement distribution differs from the distribution of this
same $\mathsf M$ on $U_T(1)A_0\rho A_0^*U_T(1)^*$ by at most $\epsilon_m$
in total variation, then for every input density operator $\rho$ the total
measured-output variation from the ideal compiled output
$A_1W_c\rho W_c^*A_1^*$ is at most
$$\epsilon_c+\epsilon_{\rm tr}+A_m(1)+\epsilon_m.$$
The transport mismatch is an explicit independent premise; the JRS estimate
bounds leakage only.
thm-qa-37-approx-encoded-two-qubit-gate:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use the six-anyon triple-triple encoding
[[def-qc-tqc-six-anyon-encoded-subspace]]. For any $U\in U(4)$ put
$$T_1=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}\in SU(5),\qquad T_\tau=U\oplus\operatorname{diag}((\det U)^{-1},1,1,1)\in SU(8).$$
For every $\delta>0$, one normalized six-strand braid word $b$ has both block
errors $\|B_1(b)-T_1\|_{\rm op}<\delta$ and
$\|B_\tau(b)-T_\tau\|_{\rm op}<\delta$. In either total-charge block, its projective logical block error and leakage
amplitude relative to the encoded action of $U$ are at most $\delta$. The physical categorical braid is
$R_1^{e(b)}B(b)$; this one common scalar is recorded under
[[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]] and must be handled under coherent control.
When the two determinant-corrected targets are supplied as certified Cauchy
inputs, the dovetailed B6 compiler finds such a word. No useful joint-block
word-length or search-time bound is asserted.
def-qa-37-fibonacci-braid-gate-set:
## Definition

Use the fixed chirality and fusion-tree basis of the three-$\tau$, total-$\tau$
Fibonacci space from [[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-qubit-matrices]]. There
$B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,r)$, $B_2=FB_1F$, and
$r=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. Put $z=e^{3\pi i/10}$ and
$$G_{\rm Fib}=\{zB_1,zB_2,(zB_1)^{-1},(zB_2)^{-1}\}\subset SU(2).$$
The determinants are one because $\det B_j=r$ and $z^2r=1$; the matrices
are unitary by the cited matrix verification. The resulting package is
inverse-closed, and its generated subgroup is dense under the inherited
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption by
[[lem-qa-37-fibonacci-su2-lifts-are-dense]]. Its exact entries are algebraic
numbers. For the finite bit implementation, the real and imaginary
coordinates are supplied by minimal polynomials over $\mathbb Q$ and rational
isolating intervals with opposite endpoint signs and exactly one real root,
as required by the finite-precision SK theorem. For the SK recursion one
additionally supplies a fixed finite base-net certificate $(\mathcal N_0,\eta_0,L_0)$ with
$0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$, as defined in
[[def-qc-inverse-closed-dense-su2-gate-set]]. The certificate is input data:
the compactness result [[lem-qc-compact-su2-base-net]] proves existence but
computes neither the list nor $L_0$.

The diagram uses the positive Artin crossing convention: time runs downward,
and the continuous left-input strand passes over the broken right-input
strand. Its word matrix is the representation convention in
[[def-qc-tqc-braid-action-from-fusion-data]]; no proof depends on the drawing.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,line width=0.8pt]
  \draw (0,2) -- (0,1.08);
  \draw (1,2) .. controls (1,1.5) and (0.72,1.25) .. (0.58,1.05);
  \draw (0.42,0.95) .. controls (0.28,0.75) and (0,0.5) .. (0,0);
  \draw (0,2) .. controls (0,1.4) and (1,0.6) .. (1,0);
  \node at (0,2.2) {$\tau$};
  \node at (1,2.2) {$\tau$};
  \node at (0,-0.25) {$\tau$};
  \node at (1,-0.25) {$\tau$};
  \node at (1.35,1) {$\sigma_i$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
def-qa-37-physical-locality-boundary:
## Definition

A **physical realization record** for a mathematical braid-compilation
instance contains, in addition to its finite fusion input and braid word, all
of: a specified physical state space and low-energy-sector identification; a
$C^2$ Hermitian path and constant-rank uniformly gapped projection; an
initial preparation isometry and its cost; a slow-time schedule; an endpoint
frame; a separately justified identification of band transport with the
chosen Fibonacci $F/R$ action and its phase; a locality model for exchanges;
and explicit preparation, excitation, measurement, and control-error terms.
The first spectral-path clauses are the finite interface in
[[def-qc-tqc-physical-braid-interface]] and
[[def-qa-37-finite-adiabatic-braid-input]]. The error ledger is
[[lem-qa-37-total-error-budget]]. A successful SK compilation, projective
density theorem, or JRS leakage estimate supplies none of the material,
locality, preparation, or band-holonomy evidence by itself; those are
independent record fields, not consequences of the mathematical compiler.
alg-qa-37-su2-solovay-kitaev-compiler:
## Definition

**Inputs:** a certified Cauchy name for an exact $S\in SU(2)$; a positive
binary-rational tolerance $\varepsilon\le\eta_0$; the fixed inverse-closed
dense Fibonacci alphabet $G_{\rm Fib}$; and a fixed certified base-net
certificate $(\mathcal N_0,\eta_0,L_0)$ with $\eta_0<64^{-2}$. Apply the
finite-precision Solovay–Kitaev recursion of
[[alg-qc-solovay-kitaev-unitary-compiler]] to this alphabet and target. Return
the resulting word in the labels $zB_1,zB_2,(zB_1)^{-1},(zB_2)^{-1}$, its
expanded length, and its Artin exponent sum $k$. For a finite Turing interface, also supply the minimal-polynomial and rational
isolating-interval descriptions of every real and imaginary gate coordinate
required by the finite-precision SK theorem. The exact-real recursion and
the finite Turing interface are distinguished: the published SK error theorem
uses exact-real comparisons, while the finite bit implementation requires the
polynomial-name and algebraic-entry hypotheses stated in
[[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]]. The base-net list is supplied
certificate data; this algorithm does not compute it from density.

**Output:** a braid word $b$ and ledger scalar $(R_1z^{-1})^k$ such that,
when the algorithm's hypotheses hold, the normalized SU(2) matrix of $b$ is
within the requested tolerance of $S$. Its physical matrix carries the
recorded scalar from [[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]].
thm-qa-37-su2-compiler-error-length:
## Statement

Let $G_{\rm Fib}$ be the fixed Fibonacci SU(2) alphabet with a supplied finite
base-net certificate of radius $0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$ and maximum word length
$L_0$. For every exact target $S\in SU(2)$ and rational
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$, let
$$\eta_{j+1}=64\eta_j^{3/2},\qquad J=\min\{j\ge0:\eta_j\le\varepsilon\}.$$
The ideal SK recursion returns a normalized braid word $W$ with
$\|S-W\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$ and length at most $L_0 5^J$; hence its
length is $O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$.
If each real and imaginary gate coordinate is supplied by its minimal
polynomial and rational isolating interval with the endpoint/root conditions
of the published finite-precision theorem, the base certificate is fixed,
and $S$ has a polynomial-time Cauchy name with query cost at most $(b+1)^c$,
the finite implementation additionally has the bit-time bound
$O((N+s_\varepsilon)^{c+10})$ from the cited theorem, where
$N=\lceil\log_2(2/\varepsilon)\rceil$ and $s_\varepsilon$ is the binary
encoding length of the rational tolerance. The lifted physical braid carries
$(R_1z^{-1})^k$ and that phase is not part of the normalized error.
thm-qa-37-arbitrary-n-encoded-circuit:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix the inverse-closed Fibonacci SU(2) gate
package and its supplied finite base-net certificate
$(\mathcal N_0,\eta_0,L_0)$ from
[[def-qa-37-fibonacci-braid-gate-set]]. Let $n\ge1$, let
$c\in\{1,\tau\}$ satisfy $V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, and let
$U\in U(2^n)$ and $\epsilon>0$. Use the arbitrary-$n$ triple code
$\mathcal C_{n,c}$, isometry $J_{n,c}$, and projector $P_{n,c}$ of
[[def-qa-37-n-triple-fusion-code]]. There exists a finite physical
Fibonacci braid word $b$ and a unit scalar $\omega$ such that
$$\|J_{n,c}^*\rho(b)J_{n,c} -\omega(U\otimes I_{V(\tau^n\to c)})\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon, \qquad \|(I-P_{n,c})\rho(b)J_{n,c}\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon.$$
The bounds are uniform over spectator fusion states. The proof composes exact
QSD, SK approximation of one-qubit SU(2) representatives, and joint B6
targets extended safely over spectators. The scalar $\omega$ is the product
of braid exponent-sum and one-qubit lift phases; under coherent control it
must be retained or corrected. For certified Cauchy target names the B6
dovetail terminates, but no useful joint-block word-length or search-time
bound follows. This is a mathematical existence result and does not imply a
physical realization.
cex-qa-37-projective-is-not-controlled:
## Statement

On one target qubit, $I_2$ and $-I_2$ differ only by a global phase and
induce the same standalone ray and outcome probabilities. Controlled access
changes the comparison. With control first,
$$C(I_2)=I_4,\qquad C(-I_2)=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&0\\0&-I_2\end{pmatrix} =Z\otimes I_2.$$
On input $|+\rangle|0\rangle$, these give $|+\rangle|0\rangle$ and
$|-\rangle|0\rangle$. Measuring the control in the $X$ basis is
respectively deterministic for $+$ and $-$, so the total-variation distance
is one. Thus projective equivalence of an isolated braid gate is not
interchangeable with equality under coherent control.
